name: Joralemon Street Tunnel
facts: The Joralemon Street Tunnel, completed in 1908, was the first underwater subway link between Manhattan and Brooklyn, stretching 6,550 feet with each tube 15.5 feet wide and descending nearly 95 feet below river level.

Designed by William Barclay Parsons, the tunnel’s steel rings were 22 inches wide, 1.125 inches thick, and covered with concrete, a pioneering construction technique that set standards for future underwater tunnels.

When it opened, the tunnel operated at speeds up to 60 miles per hour, with signal blocks as long as 2,400 feet, allowing only one train per block—a remarkable feat for early 20th‑century transit engineering.
